title: The Study Locked From the Inside
idea: classic fair-play locked-room mystery: a publisher's study locked from the inside, key on the desk; three alibis; Kiri breaks the thread-and-wax trick and the faked time

cast.name: Kiri
cast.look: a quiet sharp boy of twelve, red scarf, short messy hair, round glasses

cast.name: Hana
cast.look: his teenage cousin, green parka, long ponytail, always says what the viewer thinks

cast.name: Inspector Dale
cast.look: police inspector, long grey coat, grey moustache, notebook

cast.name: Mara
cast.look: the secretary, neat cardigan, hair in a bun, glasses on a chain

cast.name: Felix
cast.look: the nephew, leather jacket, floppy hair, a ticket stub in hand

cast.name: Dr. Voss
cast.look: the doctor, tweed jacket, bow tie, silver hair, a medical bag

scenes.title: The locked door
scenes.place: A shadowy hallway outside a heavy oak study door, a brass lamp glowing at the far end

lines.t: The study was locked from the inside. The key lay on the desk.
He never opened the door.
Aldous Crane, a publisher, went into his study at nine. At half past ten, he had not come out.
Mara knocked for ten minutes. Then we forced the door.
The window latch was shut. The only key was on his desk. Nobody could have gone in or out.
That's impossible, Kiri.
Nothing is impossible. Something is just hidden.

scenes.title: The study
scenes.place: Inside Aldous Crane's study, a dark wooden desk with a lamp, a brass key on a green blotter, a clock ticking on the shelf

lines.t: Kiri was twelve, and he rarely spoke. He looked at things the way other people listen.
He walked the room once. The desk. The key. The clock on the shelf. The door.
The desk was tidy. A cold cup of tea. A manuscript with a red pencil on top.
And a thin gap at the top of the door, no wider than a coin.
Crane's wristwatch stopped at nine-forty. So we think that is when it happened.
Stopped. But the clock on the shelf is still running.
So? Different clocks.
Remember that. Remember the watch.

scenes.title: Dr. Voss
scenes.place: The grand hallway of Crane's house at night, a medical bag on a chair beside a hall telephone

lines.t: Three people were in the house that night. Each of them has an alibi.
First, Dr. Voss, Crane's doctor. He came at nine for a check-up and left the study at twenty past.
He was well. Cheerful, even. I said goodnight in the hall.
At nine-forty I phoned the hospital from this very phone. The switchboard keeps a log.
A bag of medicine bottles, a spool of blue thread, a stick of red sealing wax. A doctor's tools.
A phone log. That's solid.

scenes.title: Mara
scenes.place: A busy farmhouse kitchen at night, a cook stirring a pot, silver spoons laid out on a long table

lines.t: Second, Mara, the secretary. She has worked for Crane for six years.
From nine to ten I counted the silver with Mrs. Pell, the cook. We never left the kitchen.
He told me to take the morning off. He said he would write me a letter.
He never said what was in it.
The cook agrees. Mara found the door locked at half past ten and called the police.
Another alibi. Everyone is covered.
Not yet. Keep counting.

scenes.title: Felix
scenes.place: A small village cinema lobby, a ticket booth, a red ticket stub in a young man's hand

lines.t: Third, Felix, Crane's nephew. He has money troubles, and an uncle who refused to help.
We argued at supper. I left at ten to nine and walked straight to the cinema.
A man with a motive and an alibi. Interesting.
I was at the village cinema from nine. Here is my ticket. The usher saw me all night.
The ticket says nine o'clock. The usher confirms it.
Three people, three alibis, one locked room. I do not like it, Kiri.
I do. It means someone made a plan.

scenes.title: Three clues
scenes.place: A close view of the study door frame and the desk, with a magnifying glass hovering over a tiny spot of red wax

lines.t: Now look closely. Three clues are in plain view. Each one is named once.
Nobody touched the room. The police photographed everything, and the three clues sat there the whole time.
One. A tiny drop of red wax on the door frame, level with the lock.
Two. A blue fibre caught on the ring of the key.
Three. A wristwatch stopped at nine-forty, glass unbroken, while the clock on the shelf still runs.
Pause the video if you want to guess. Who made a plan?

scenes.title: The wax
scenes.place: A close view of the door frame, a drop of red wax shining beside a small iron latch bar

lines.t: The wax first. The only red sealing wax in this house is in one bag.
And nobody drips wax on a door frame by accident.
The doctor's bag?
Let's see what else it explains.

scenes.title: The thread
scenes.place: A close view of the brass key on the green blotter, a single blue fibre across its ring

lines.t: The fibre. Not wool, not cotton. Blue nylon thread, the kind in a spool.
A spool like the one in the doctor's bag. Mara's drawer has only white thread. Felix owns none.
So the thread touched the key.
And the key was never in the lock. Why would a thread go through its ring?

scenes.title: The watch
scenes.place: A close view of Crane's silver wristwatch on the desk, the hands stopped, the glass shining and whole

lines.t: Now the watch. Stopped at nine-forty, with an unbroken glass.
A fall would crack it. So someone stopped it by hand, and chose the time.
Who needs it to be nine-forty? Only someone who is safe at nine-forty.
Felix was in the cinema from nine. Mara was in the kitchen from nine. They are safe at any hour that matters.
Dr. Voss left the study at twenty past nine. His only alibi starts at nine-forty.
So the watch was moved to hide the true time.

scenes.title: The trick
scenes.place: A re-enactment drawing of the study door from the outside, a long blue thread running from the latch bar through a key ring to a wax guide on the frame

lines.t: Here is how the door was locked. Step one. A latch bar inside the door, lifted, with a thread tied to it.
Step two. The thread runs through the ring of the key.
Then it passes over a drop of wax, a small guide, and out through the gap above the door.
Step three. Outside, pull the thread. The key is a weight. The bar drops, and the door is fast.
Step four. Let go. The thread slips out through the gap, dragged by the falling key, which lands on the desk.
It leaves a fibre on the ring, and a drop of wax on the frame.
A harmless trick with a thread, a weight and a bar. And all of it was in plain view.
So the door was never locked from inside at all.
It only looked locked. Anyone can fool a door. It is much harder to fool a clock.

scenes.title: The hall
scenes.place: The hallway again at dawn, the medical bag open on a chair and a spool of blue thread on top

lines.t: Dr. Voss, open your bag.
The spool was blue. The thread matched the fibre. The wax matched the drop.
This is ridiculous. I was on the phone at nine-forty.
You were. But Mr. Crane was already silent, and the clock on the shelf is the only honest clock in the room.
A thread? Half the village owns blue thread!
Half the village does not own that wax. Or a watch that stops at the very hour you need.

scenes.title: Why
scenes.place: A quiet study at sunrise, a manuscript on the desk with a single page lifted by the draught

lines.t: The motive is two lines long. Crane was about to print a story about Voss.
It said the work that made the doctor famous was never his own.
Dr. Voss confessed in the hall. Mara cried, and Felix could not speak.
He did not want the world to read it. So he planned a door nobody could open.
All because of a thread.
Which clue did you notice first?
